#3008. If Inflation Stays Hot, These 5 ETFs Could Be Smart Buys

No ETF is a guaranteed hedge against inflation, but some are built to be more effective.

By Dana George – Nov 23, 2026 at 3:45PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Schwab Strategic Trust - Schwab U.s. Tips ETF ›

If you fill your gas tank or buy groceries, you undoubtedly understand how inflation erodes the purchasing power of cash. And if you invest, you may be on the lookout for assets that can help cushion your portfolio.

While no exchange-traded fund (ETF) is a guaranteed inflation shield, some do a better job than others at protecting your portfolio. Here are five of them.

SCHP invests in Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS). The principal adjusts with inflation, helping preserve purchasing power, and pays interest on that adjusted principal.

TIPS can help preserve purchasing power over time. However, a TIPS value may fluctuate if market prices fall.

VTIP is a shorter-duration alternative. During inflationary times, VTIP may be less sensitive to interest rate changes than funds holding longer-term bonds because it focuses on shorter-maturity TIPS.

If you seek inflation-linked bonds with less duration risk, VTIP is worth considering. Keep in mind, though, the fund still carries risk, and returns depend on both inflation adjustments and changes in bond prices.

Switching to yet another kind of exposure, PDBC invests in commodity futures across markets, such as agriculture, metals, and energy. Commodities are closely tied to costs that often drive inflation, so they may perform well when raw material prices rise.

However, commodity prices can swing sharply, and futures-based funds naturally face complexities that you may not be accustomed to.

Gold is viewed as a way to preserve wealth over time. Unlike cash, it can't be created at will, and gold may rise in value as cash loses purchasing power. Gold can also help balance a portfolio loaded with stocks and bonds.

On the downside, gold is not directly tied to the CPI and can fall even while inflation remains elevated. In addition, its performance may lag when interest-bearing assets become more attractive.

Still, investing in GLDM is one way to diversify risk.

XLE holds energy sector companies, so if oil and gas prices rise, the fund's value may rise, making it a hedge against inflation.Yet energy stocks are still stocks, and regulation, company costs, demand, and even market sentiment can outweigh the effect of higher fuel prices.

While each of these funds can be a great addition to your portfolio as inflation heats up, they're not interchangeable. SCHP and VTIP focus on inflation-linked government bonds, while PDBC tracks a collection of commodity futures. GLDM provides gold exposure, while XLE invests in energy companies.

Each ETF responds to inflation through a different mechanism, and while each can help, they can all disappoint if the market moves the other way.

The takeaway is to treat inflation-focused ETFs as possible portfolio pieces rather than all-in solutions. Before investing, consider fees, diversification, tax treatment, and how much volatility you can tolerate.

#3007. Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

With Agent 365 Business Analytics, Microsoft could reshape enterprise spending, but there's a critical difference between estimated value and money saved.

We all know AI can get expensive. But does that expense result in real business value? That’s the trillion-dollar question Microsoft aims to answer with today’s introduction of Agent 365 Business Analytics.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost

Earlier this year, Microsoft introduced Agent 365, its tool for tracking agents the way an HR department would normally track human employees. With Agent 365 Business Analytics, Microsoft is attempting to build an accounting system for AI labor. The system attempts to calculate the economic value of the work performed by agents compared with what the agents cost, and then provide a return on investment estimate.

If it works, this is some very cool stuff. Microsoft is trying to map labor-market economics onto AI usage data to create value estimates.

Also: Work IQ is Microsoft’s big bet on agent-first enterprise IT, and I have questions

To do so, it uses real labor-costing information, including data from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, the O*NET database from the US Department of Labor, and its own LinkedIn Occupational Graph.

This data, along with data gathered from Agent 365, is aggregated into analysis intended to answer:

The goal is to provide a comprehensive picture of AI spend against value produced.

Software accounting is long established and straightforward. We measure subscription fees, cost per seat, compute costs, burden costs (like floor space and other infrastructure), and more. But AI work doesn’t fit that model, making it very hard to quantify value.

Instead, Agent 365 Business Analytics measures cost both relative to human labor and in terms of technological expense. For example, it might look at a task and determine how much human effort that task would normally take, and then price that effort based on prevailing common labor rates.

Then, it might factor in how much of the task was actually done by a human vs. how much was contributed by an AI, along with the estimated value of the AI’s contribution. Then it mixes in the actual AI processing cost (whether in subscriptions, tokens, on-premises infrastructure, and cloud support).

Also: These Claude Enterprise features let you track AI ROI – what’s new

What comes out is a hybrid labor estimate that combines human contribution, human-replacement savings, AI costs, and then potentially AI savings over human costs. It sounds positively Orwellian. But the bottom line is that companies really haven’t been able to understand the AI bottom line.

There’s a catch. All these numbers are estimates. In its blog post, Redmond specifically says, “Assisted hours are a directional estimate of work AI helped complete, not measured time saved or financial return.”

In other words, what Agent 365 Business Analytics estimates might not actually line up with real-world experience or expenses. It’s also possible that AI work might have been assigned because there was AI to do the work, not that the AI was saving company labor costs with every token processed.

In other words, Microsoft may be able to tell you the economic value of AI-assisted work, but it can’t demonstrate definitively that the company saved any real money.

Also: 5 reasons your company needs a chief AI officer in 2026

I find it particularly telling that this is from the company that makes PowerPoint. Because now, with Agent 365 Business Analytics, it’s entirely possible that you could produce economic dashboards that look really, really impressive, but are entirely irrelevant to real life.

That’s not to say the product is useless. But it does go to the idea that you will have to be quite disciplined in how you interpret the results and how much stock you put in them for decision-making. It is one source of possible truth, not the source of absolute truth.

Microsoft has been investing for decades to build out the core infrastructure of enterprise computing. AI isn’t any different when it comes to the company’s overall mission.

With Agent 365 and the company’s related offerings, Microsoft wants to help you:

This means the company doesn’t necessarily have to provide you with the AI model to help you run your enterprise. With integration with offerings from OpenAI, Anthropic, Salesforce, Google, Databricks, Snowflake, and others, the company doesn’t even have to provide the apps or SaaS capabilities.

But if it can get in there and manage your plumbing, help you control costs, and be the HR operation for your AI workforce, Microsoft could own a central piece of your business’s operations.

#3006. Are We There Yet? NASA’s Escapade Is Heading to Mars in a ‘Pioneering’ Maneuver

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

No space agency has ever staged spacecraft in orbit for a year before sending them on to Mars.

NASA launched its Escapade mission just over a year ago to send two spacecraft, nicknamed Blue and Gold, to Mars. After spending a year looping near Earth, the twin probes completed a gravity-assist maneuver this month and are now en route to the red planet.

It’s an exciting time for NASA. Blue and Gold, named for the school colors of UC Berkeley where they were built, completed the agency’s first powered Earth flyby.

Typically, spacecraft use a planet’s or the sun’s gravity to get close to the planet before slingshotting off into the distance. A notable example is Voyager 1, which used unpowered gravity-assisted flybys to reach the speeds needed to cross the light-day threshold earlier this week. Escapade did this with Earth’s gravity but also used thrusters to generate even more speed. Since there are two of them, NASA personnel had to perform this maneuver twice.

The other big win for NASA is that Mars will soon have two additional satellites in orbit to measure the planet’s magnetosphere, which is believed to have been stripped by the solar wind eons ago, when the planet likely had liquid water.

These satellites are notable for being NASA’s first low-cost mission to Mars, costing the agency approximately $75 million as part of the Small Innovative Missions for Planetary Exploration program. It also marked the debut of Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket for a space mission, and the company was able to achieve the first vertical landing of its rocket after sending Escapade on its way.

Escapade still has a long way to go. Blue and Gold are now spending the next 10 months flying into outer space. Their new trajectory is set to take them into Mars’ orbital path, timed in such a way that the twin satellites will arrive at the same time that Mars naturally shows up, allowing the red planet to capture the twins in its orbit as it flies by. NASA says that both are set to arrive at Mars by early September next year.

By the time the twins get there, they will have been in space for 22 months. Flights to Mars require months of deep space travel, impeccable timing and loads of fuel. However, if missions hit specific launch windows, they require far less fuel.

This is a well-documented maneuver known as the Hohmann Transfer, and NASA’s JPL has a neat math exercise to show how it’s calculated. NASA intentionally launched Escapade a year early so that the satellites could hang out in a gravitational sweet spot called the L2 Earth-Sun Lagrange point. This is a point in space on the side of the Earth opposite the sun, and the idea was to have the spacecraft already in orbit and ready for the next Mars launch window.

Once it opened, the satellites engaged their thrusters, performed a gravity-assisted flyby of Earth to gain speed, and launched themselves into outer space.

The tactic of sending Escapade to the L2 Lagrange point to wait for a Mars window to open is arguably NASA’s biggest win, as no space agency has ever attempted it. The benefit is that it allows agencies to launch payloads into orbit bound for Mars whenever they have the time, then use Earth gravity assists to slingshot them out to Mars when it’s most efficient.

“With this loiter orbit and Earth flyby, Escapade is pioneering a new strategy for getting to Mars,” Jeff Parker, CTO of Advanced Space and lead mission designer, said in a statement. “This method provides the flexibility to launch almost anytime and then use Earth’s gravity to get a boost to Mars, rather than waiting every two years to launch there directly when the planets are aligned.”

The maneuver paid dividends. JAXA, Japan’s national space agency, launched its MMX spacecraft on Oct. 20, which is within the current Mars launch window and employs the same Hohmann Transfer method to get to Mars. The spacecraft is headed to Phobos and Deimos, Mars’s moons.

Despite using the more traditional method of waiting for the window to open to launch, JAXA’s MMX is slated to reach its destination in August next year, just a couple of weeks ahead of Escapade. When you factor in that Escapade performed its gravity-assist slingshot on Nov. 9, roughly two weeks before MMX launched, the spacecraft will reach their respective destinations in approximately the same amount of time, validating NASA’s trajectory strategy.

Microsoft is bridging the gap between proprietary and open-weight AI while targeting data-conscious businesses.

During the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced several new models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the company. But new model releases are almost a dime a dozen these days, and accelerating fast — what really stood out was how Microsoft will let its customers access those models.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5

MAI said it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights. It’s essentially a selective approach to open-weight AI: more so than proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, but not fully downloadable on Hugging Face like Mistral’s Le Chonk. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account reps to get started.

“You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay entirely yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Company to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents,” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of MAI, said during the keynote.

The dominant, if simplified, narrative in AI has been that proprietary, expensive models boast peak capabilities but aren’t customizable, while open, cheaper models are customizable but less capable. Microsoft’s AI models don’t necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the company has legacy sway with countless businesses. By offering a customizable AI option, it could strike a balance among major tech companies.

Western labs, including Thinking Machines and Mistral, are releasing more competitive open-weight models, but Anthropic and OpenAI still have the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Though Licensed Weights isn’t an open-weight family of models, it does diversify the open-versus-closed debate a bit and differentiate Microsoft’s offering from OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s. It’s also a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal to balance price and performance, if businesses find it impressive enough.

The company also released its new image editing model, MAI Image 2.7, on Tuesday, which now leads the category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft has positioned itself for organizations seeking a reliable blend of ROI tools, customization, security controls, and capability.

#2997. Why You Shouldn’t Use Meta’s Muse AI Agent for Shopping Next Weekend

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

It’s been over two months since Meta debuted its Muse AI agent, giving people new tools to automate tasks like handling email replies, booking travel or even shopping for you.

That’s especially the case when it comes to handing over sensitive financial information. If you give an AI access to your digital wallets to shop for you, the risk extends beyond an authorized purchase. You could be exposing your bank accounts to a potential security breach or data exposure, with little recourse to fix it. If you were considering letting Muse make decisions and transactions with your money ahead of Black Friday and Cyber Monday, you should know it’s still raising red flags as a shopping companion.

Despite the risk, Muse has remained popular and now faces competition from Anthropic’s newly released Claude Duet, another AI business agent. Meta is also releasing a $300 portable device, Charm, in a virtual-toy style that will work with Muse.

A representative for Meta has not responded to CNET’s request for comment.

Muse asks for the keys to your digital life: passwords, full disk access, emails, calendar invites, contacts, Notes and WhatsApp chats. Meta also feeds your conversations into its AI training pipeline by default, leaving it on you to dig through the settings and opt out.

More recently, Meta employees themselves have flagged instances where Muse may have accessed encrypted messages from apps such as Signal or information from other Muse users, which Meta has chalked up to “isolated incidents” and that permission to access apps and information from notifications has to be explicitly granted in a statement to news outlets.

If the previous incidents weren’t enough to give you pause, there’s also a widely publicized case in which Muse mistakenly shared the home address of a Toronto tech reviewer, Matt Robb, with a potential buyer on Facebook Marketplace. Muse invited the stranger to Robb’s home without his explicit consent or knowledge, then later apologized for doing so, as detailed in a Threads post. Robb hadn’t realized that he had inadvertently granted Muse blanket permission to automatically reply to Marketplace inquiries using the details he provided, including his address.

Before facing a potential security nightmare, here are a few other things to know about Muse.

Muse uploads iOS or Mac data even when you tell it not to: Meta’s Muse appears to blatantly ignore user permissions, according to a September report by AppleInsider. In one case, the AI agent synced roughly 187,000 lines of a user’s Apple Messages without their consent, even though “Full Disk Access” was turned off. The report shows that Muse pinged a user’s messages database thousands of times despite disk access being disabled. Muse then successfully harvested texts from the user’s Mac — not from Meta’s Messenger, but from Apple Messages. Even people who refuse to use Muse may have their data collected by the AI if they text someone who does have it installed.

Muse could hand over data to human callers: Before Meta launched the ability for its Muse to make outbound business calls on your behalf, internal Meta documents revealed that the company planned to rely on human contractors at call centers to help make reservations and appointments. That means not only would the software have access to all your private data, but a total stranger might also be managing your personal commitments — all without your knowledge. The human concierge feature appears to have been rolled back for now, according to Reuters.

Muse has the most robust data collection: In September, the VPN company Surfshark said it found that Meta Muse is collecting — or attempting to collect — 31 out of 35 types of data, putting it far ahead of other popular chatbots like Gemini, ChatGPT and DeepSeek. Muse also collects highly sensitive personal information like location data, sexual orientation, genetic information or biometric data. Muse (along with Meta AI and Gemini) also reserves the right to use collected audio data for other purposes, such as analytics or product personalization. Surfshark released a full dataset of what it uncovered.

Meta has tried hard with Muse to make the AI agent seem cute and approachable, but when it comes to your money and giving Muse access to it, it’s best to be very cautious for the time being.

#2994. Google Is Killing the Nest App. Here’s What Comes Next

Don't panic: All your devices should transfer over to Google Home fairly seamlessly.

Google Home is replacing Nest and bringing new devices.

If you’re a Nest smart home user, a major change is coming in early 2027 that will affect how you manage your smart home. Google has confirmed to CNET via email that both the Nest app and Google Assistant are being retired, and current users will lose access to both next year.

All Nest devices will lose Nest app support in favor of the Google Home app, and the Nest app will be retired on Jan. 25, 2027. Google Assistant will be removed from home devices on Aug. 2, 2027, with all support moving to the Gemini for Home voice assistant.

The change is part of Google’s effort to consolidate its various apps and devices into a single app and voice experience. In a statement sent to CNET, Google confirmed that “every device supported today works with these updated experiences.”

Nest Thermostats should all seamlessly port over to Google Home.

Google has confirmed that Google Home will support all your Nest devices, including thermostats, cameras, doorbells, smoke detectors and locks. Existing schedules and settings should transfer over automatically, which is often a hassle when you switch between apps and devices. You should also be able to pair your Nest devices with any Works with Google Home and Matter smart home devices, as well as Google Home speakers and smart displays and TV streamers, all with the same app.

As part of the switchover, you should be able to access Nest devices on various platforms outside of the mobile app. It’ll support iOS and Android widgets, the Home Panel on Android, smart displays, speakers and the Google Home web page. That includes being able to check live camera views, adjust your thermostat and lock your front door, right from a TV or smartwatch.

Google Assistant may be leaving, but Google is releasing newer, more powerful devices.

However, to continue controlling and receiving notifications from your Nest devices remotely, you will need to switch to the Google Home app or home.google.com if you prefer to control them via a web browser.

You can change Google voice assistant voices, but not the wake words.

On Aug. 2, 2027, Gemini for Home voice assistant will fully replace Google Assistant on speakers and smart displays. The switch to Gemini makes a lot of sense if you’ve used Google Assistant at all. Assistant is very much an older voice assistant, lacking the smarter follow-ups and natural-language capabilities that make Gemini more useful.With Gemini, you should get answers to more complex questions, and you can speak more naturally without barking commands, letting it handle conversation context and remember multiple interactions.

Getting ready for Google Home is easy, though Google has an entire Nest App Transition Support Hub if you need step-by-step instructions to walk you through everything that’s needed.

For most people, it should be a simple matter of downloading the Google Home app. Naturally, a Google Account is required, but as mentioned, your Nest devices, including the cameras and video history, will automatically transfer from the Nest app starting on Jan. 25, 2027.

Gemini’s Google Home integrations are useful, but command options can include some risks.

The other thing you may have to do is download any custom video clips you’ve created on home.nest.com. Manually saved clips won’t transfer to the Google Home app along with your video history. To make sure these are backed up, you’ll want to visit home.nest.com before Jan. 25, 2027, and use the Download All button to save clips you want to keep.

The final deadline to migrate your Nest account to a Google account before the company starts data deletions March 25, 2027.

Google says Nest devices, including cameras and video history, will automatically transfer from the Nest app to the Google Home app. Nest Aware (1st Gen) subscriptions should also automatically switch to Google Home Premium so that coverage continues without interruption. Google Home Premium is replacing Nest Aware (1st Gen), and users will receive an email closer to the transfer date detailing your subscription information.

Google’s smart displays should all work perfectly with the various Nest devices.

Gemini for Home is already available in many countries and languages. Google announced earlier that it’s expanding to more regions over the coming months. Users in a supported region can upgrade to Gemini Home right now.

On your phone, open the latest version of the Google Home app, tap your profile icon in the top right to open Home Settings, then tap “Get Started” on the “Set up Gemini for Home” banner. On your computer, just visit home.google.com/gemini.

#2993. Zscaler Stock Surged on CrowdStrike's $43.9 Billion Buyout. Here's How Much Shareholders Will Actually Get

CrowdStrike is paying for Zscaler in its own stock, and that stock fell almost 10% the day the deal was announced.

By Jonathan Ponciano – Nov 23, 2026 at 3:58PM EST

10 stocks we like better than CrowdStrike ›

CrowdStrike (CRWD -8.92%) announced on Monday that it will buy Zscaler (ZS +17.67%) in an all-stock deal valued at about $43.9 billion. The press release put the offer at $260.41 per Zscaler share, a 34% premium to Friday's close.

But Zscaler holders won't receive $260.41 in cash. They will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each Zscaler share, a fixed ratio that rises and falls with CrowdStrike's price. The $260.41 figure comes from CrowdStrike's Friday close of $229.44.

By 3:30 p.m. ET Monday, CrowdStrike had dropped 9.6% to $207.45. At that price, 1.135 shares are worth about $235.45, roughly $25 less than the headline number. Zscaler traded at $227.45, up 16.8% on the day but still $8 below the deal's current value.

CrowdStrike reported its third-quarter results alongside the deal. Revenue rose 28% to $1.58 billion. Net new annual recurring revenue reached a record $419 million, and total annual recurring revenue grew 27% to $6.26 billion.

The stock fell anyway, losing about $22 billion in market value, which is half the price CrowdStrike agreed to pay. Paying in stock means CrowdStrike's current shareholders give up part of the company: they will own about 84.1% of the combined business, and Zscaler's holders 15.9%.

CrowdStrike says the deal will add about $1 billion in annual revenue within 30 months of closing and cut about $500 million in yearly costs within 18 to 24 months. It plans to sell its Falcon products to about 8,000 Zscaler customers that don't use CrowdStrike today.

The merger filing needs approval from Zscaler shareholders and antitrust regulators. The companies expect to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal 2028, which runs from August 2027 to January 2028. Either side can walk away if the deal hasn't closed by Nov. 23, 2027, a date that moves to Feb. 23, 2028, if only antitrust or foreign-investment reviews remain.

Founder and CEO Jay Chaudhry and his affiliates, who hold about 34% of Zscaler's shares, have agreed to vote in favor of the deal. Zscaler would owe CrowdStrike a $1.4 billion fee if it walked away for a better offer.

A 3.5% gap for a wait of a year or more is small, which suggests traders expect the deal to close. It also means Zscaler's stock now mostly tracks CrowdStrike's. Anyone buying Zscaler at $227 is effectively betting on CrowdStrike's price in late 2027 among cybersecurity stocks, and that price has already fallen 26% from its 52-week closing high of $278.86 on Oct. 6.

Zscaler holders who want to own the combined company can hold on. Those who bought Zscaler for its own business should know that, if the deal closes, they will end up owning CrowdStrike stock.

#2991. With Mortgage Rates Rising, Should You Hibernate Until Spring?

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. While we don't cover every company or financial product on the market, we work hard to share a wide range of offers and objective editorial perspectives.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us for advertisements that appear on our site. This compensation helps us provide tools and services - like free credit score access and monitoring. With the exception of mortgage, home equity and other home-lending products or services, partner compensation is one of several factors that may affect which products we highlight and where they appear on our site. Other factors include your credit profile, product availability and proprietary website methodologies.

However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

Higher borrowing costs aren't the whole story. Here's what to consider before putting your house hunt on hold.

Mortgage rates are back up this week, wiping out modest relief from a monthlong drop that began in mid-October.

The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up 29 basis points to 7.28% APR in the week ending Nov. 19, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.) We calculate our weekly average using daily APRs recorded over the past five business days.

A mortgage is a big ol’ loan, so when rates go up, those fractions of a percentage point add up fast. Say you’re borrowing $400,000 on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage. Compared with last week, your monthly principal and interest payment would be about $78 higher today.

One bad week doesn't make a trend, but a jump like this can make putting your house hunt on hold until spring feel like a safer bet. So … is it?

Before deciding whether to buy a house now or wait, it helps to know what's pushing mortgage rates higher.

Right now, mortgage rates are still feeling the aftershocks from two major inflation reports last week. First, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) showed consumer prices rose more than expected in October. Then, the Producer Price Index (PPI) showed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its biggest annual increase in nearly four years.

While CPI shows how prices have changed, PPI can offer clues about what's coming next. Faced with higher costs, businesses may raise their own prices to compensate, keeping inflation elevated. Federal Reserve policymakers aren't expecting much relief anytime soon, either. According to meeting minutes released Nov. 18, they expect inflation to remain elevated above their 2% target for a while.

To cool rising prices, the Fed can raise the federal funds rate, which is the benchmark interest rate banks charge each other for overnight loans. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. A rate hike is widely expected at the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting.

Even after a Fed rate hike, there’s no telling how quickly inflation will cool — or whether mortgage rates will follow. (Inflation is just one of many forces that affect mortgage rates, after all.) So if you do wait until spring to buy a house, don't do it just because you're betting on a cheaper mortgage.

If you're not in a rush to move, winter can be a good time to regroup. Fewer homes typically go up for sale from November through February, so waiting until spring could give you more options.

But new data from the National Association of Realtors suggests this year's slowdown goes beyond the usual seasonal lull. High mortgage rates and home prices are making it tough for many buyers to make the numbers work. For some buyers, waiting isn't a strategy — it's the only option.

Pending home sales, a measure of homes under contract, fell 16.7% in October compared with a year earlier, NAR reports. All four U.S. regions saw declines. At this rate, NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun warned that annual home sales could fall to their lowest level since the mid-1990s.

“Either sizable housing demand is building in the background, or the dream of homeownership is increasingly out of reach for many Americans,” Yun said in a news release.

Whether you're waiting by choice or necessity, you can use the time to strengthen your finances. Paying down debt, strengthening your credit score or saving for a bigger down payment could help you qualify for a better mortgage deal.

Every little bit helps when today’s mortgage rates are this high.

Mortgage preapprovals typically expire after 60 to 90 days. If you're already preapproved, why not keep an eye on listings this winter? (Hey, I’m an optimist. All it takes is one house.)

Think like a seller for a second. If you're listing your house in the dead of winter, you're probably not doing it just for fun. You might have a deadline, and you’re probably more willing to negotiate. In the winter, buyers have less competition — and more room to negotiate a lower price, closing cost credits or repairs. Those savings on the sticker price might help offset today's higher borrowing costs.

Spring typically brings more homes for sale, but it also brings more buyers competing for them. And if mortgage rates end up dropping this spring, you won't be the only one coming out of hibernation.

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

The search giant is revamping Google.com with AI options.

This is not your parents’ Google home page. In its push to get more users to adopt its AI tools, the search engine giant is rolling out a raft of new features worldwide.

The new elements include three new buttons below the search bar at Google.com: Create images, Ask about files and Brainstorm. The Google Search button is gone, but the I’m Feeling Lucky button remains.

The buttons are available when using Google on a desktop but not on mobile. I was able to see the new buttons when signed in to my Google account.

When signed out, I was only able to see the typical home page, with the only AI button being AI Mode, which has been there since May 2025.

Clicking on the “Create images” button opens up a new page where you can create an AI-generated image using Google’s Nano Banana. It’s the same image-generation tool you can use on other Google platforms such as the Gemini app, Google AI Studio and AI Mode in Search.

Clicking “Ask about files” allows for several options. You can have the AI analyze a document and rewrite it, simply have it answer questions or ask it to perform tasks such as “polish my resume” or “draft an email with action items.”

The “Brainstorm” button prompts you to “describe your goal,” such as making a to-do list, learning how to code or finding a table at a restaurant.

Another new feature, as announced by Google Search Product VP Robby Stein on X, is a collapsible sidebar on the left side of the home page, which shows your recent AI search threads and offers the ability to create a new one:

Stein said the new sidebar will help users go back to where they left off.

“People are coming to Search with more questions that aren’t just one and done — and in testing, this sidebar made a big difference for making progress & continuing to explore the web,” Stein posted.

I didn’t see the collapsible sidebar during my testing of the home page.

Google has integrated its Gemini AI models throughout its various platforms — Search, Gmail, Docs, Pixel phones and third-party apps such as Adobe, Shopify, OpenTable and Instacart. This past week, Google announced several other new AI features — integrations with stores such as Albertsons, Safeway and Target to complete orders and connect to apps such as Peloton and Adobe.

Over the summer, Google’s Gemini app topped 1 billion users in what CEO Sundar Pichai called the company’s “fastest growing product ever.”

But Google’s rush to force-feed AI into its products has met with plenty of pushback. The New York City, Los Angeles and Chicago school districts said they might choose different search engines because Google said it will not remove AI from search tools used by students, The New York Times reported.

Google said search and the Gemini app will be turned off for schools unless school administrators want them. But Google said there will not be a chatbot-free version of search available for schools. So schools declining AI will not be able to search using Google at all.

Google’s AI Overviews, which appear at the top of many search page results, have also been blamed for a steep drop in web traffic to content publishers. AI Overviews summarize user search queries and replace the long list of blue hyperlinks that once appeared across search pages. So instead of clicking on those links to get more information, giving publishers valuable clicks, a user can simply get their query response by reading the AI Overview.

#2987. FormFactor: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Cost discipline is protecting margins even as customers shift orders, a sign the company can sustain profitability.

By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 23, 2026 at 4:00PM EST

10 stocks we like better than FormFactor ›

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, FormFactor (FORM +11.71%) delivered its fourth consecutive quarter of record revenues and raised its baseline non-GAAP gross margin to 53%. The semiconductor test equipment supplier is benefiting from expanding demand in artificial intelligence applications, but existing plants are running at maximum capacity.

Existing manufacturing facilities are operating at their output limits, making the new factory in Farmers Branch, Texas, critical for meeting customer demand. The site expands production of probe cards, which are specialized test interfaces used to inspect semiconductor wafers before packaging.

Dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) customers shifted orders toward standard DDR5 memory chips to capture higher market prices. Internal manufacturing cost reduction programs kept probe card profitability high despite lower volumes of high-bandwidth memory cards.

High-performance computing relies increasingly on co-packaged optics (CPO), a technique using light instead of electricity to transfer data between microchips. Demand for TRITON optical testing systems accelerated throughout 2026 as chipmakers adopted the technology.

Demand for advanced test systems is accelerating across graphics processing units (GPUs), central processing units (CPUs), and application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs). Broad exposure across chip architectures provides multiple growth vectors while new factory capacity comes online.

Factory efficiency gains and disciplined operating expenses are expanding operating leverage as annual revenues approach $1 billion.

#2986. New Hyundai Elantra Hybrid Debuts With 53 Mpg, AI in the Dash

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

The redesigned compact sedan features Hyundai’s new AI voice assistant, Gleo AI, and an updated regenerative braking system with EV-like one-pedal driving.

Hyundai pulled back the cover on the new 2027 Elantra sedan and 2028 Elantra Hybrid this week at the LA Auto Show, and, wow, it looks like nothing else in its class. The bold styling may not be for everyone — though, personally, I dig it — but economy car shoppers will certainly be interested in the compact hybrid sedan’s targeted 53 mpg and Gleo, Hyundai’s new AI voice assistant that controls the automaker’s new Android Automotive OS-based dashboard tech.

The humble Hyundai Elantra hasn’t historically been a sexy car, but it remains an important one for the brand. It’s the automaker’s second-bestselling vehicle, behind only the Tucson. More importantly, the Elantra is one of the stalwarts of the affordable compact sedan class, a segment that many US automakers have abandoned in favor of more profitable SUVs. At a time when buyers are more sensitive than ever to inflated fuel costs and sticker prices, economy car options like the Elantra and its second-generation hybrid powertrain are worth our attention.

The updated hybrid powertrain pairs a 1.6-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine with a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox. Combined output at the front wheels rises to 155 horsepower (up from 139 hp in the current car), thanks to a more powerful 45-kilowatt electric-assist motor (up from 32kW).

An updated regenerative braking system recaptures energy when slowing and now offers an “EV-like one-pedal driving experience” that can bring the car to a complete stop at its maximum setting. Additionally, the hybrid now features a new Stay mode that lets the climate control and infotainment systems run while parked for up to 30 minutes without firing up the gas engine.

Sharing the stage in LA, the new nonhybrid Elantra arrives with the same 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine and continuously variable transmission as the current generation. At 147 hp with a target of 35 mpg combined, it’s no more powerful than before, but it should also be no less efficient, despite the sedan’s increased size. I’d say the hybrid is the better choice, though it will likely also be the more expensive powertrain option.

Inside, a new cockpit design moves the now-hoodless digital instrument cluster, a 9.9-inch “Slim Information Display,” away from the driver and toward the windshield on the dashboard. The new placement, similar to what I’ve seen on recent Toyota models, puts vehicle information closer to the driver’s line of sight.

Pleos Connect, Hyundai’s new Android Automotive OS-based infotainment suite, lives on a 12.9-inch center display. Despite being based on Android, it still features the automaker’s bespoke navigation and media software, rather than Google Maps. The system is said to be over-the-air updatable and features standard wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto for drivers who’d rather bring their own apps on the road.

The Pleos dashboard OS is matched with Gleo AI (who names these things?!), which is Hyundai’s new AI voice assistant that lets drivers and passengers talk to the car rather than occupy a hand on the touchscreen. Hyundai says the system features “contextual language support, multi-command capability and zone-specific recognition,” which basically means the car knows who’s talking to it and which seat they’re in and can assign context to voice prompts based on the situation.

“Affordable doesn’t have to be anonymous,” said Olabisi Boyle, Hyundai’s senior vice president of product, at the unveiling. I agree: Hyundai’s designers clearly aren’t afraid to push the design envelope, and the new Elantra is anything but bland.

The sedan introduces the automaker’s Art of Steel design language, with chunky flared fenders that feel inspired by the brand’s recent new SUVs. The tall greenhouse looks a bit cartoonish if you catch it at the wrong angle, but it provides increased headroom inside. From certain angles, the sedan’s beefy fenders remind me of an angular Korean take on the Subaru WRX. From other viewpoints, I can see inspiration from Hyundai’s N Vision 74 concept and the hydrogen-fueled Nexo, particularly in the triangular rear windows.

The sedan measures 188.8 inches bumper-to-bumper on a 108.3-inch wheelbase that is 1.2 inches longer than the current model’s. Hyundai says the stretch for this generation improves rear-passenger space, now rated at 39.1 inches of legroom on the second row. The Elantra, according to its designers, now approaches the interior volume of a midsize car, a claim I’d take with a grain of salt had I not watched multiple six-foot-plus attendees slip into the back seat with relative ease.

Hyundai did not announce pricing or detailed specs at the auto show debut, and availability is still vague. However, based on the stated model years, which are usually slightly offset from calendar years, I expect the 2027 Elantra sedan to arrive in early 2027, with the 2028 Elantra Hybrid following in late 2027.

Editors’ note: Antuan Goodwin’s travel costs were covered by Genesis. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

Apple's redesigned Health app arrives in December with some major upgrades, but not every iPhone will get the full experience.

Apple is kicking off a new and improved Health app next month with the release of iOS 27.3. Instead of just recording and displaying your health-related stats, the app will tap into Apple Intelligence to analyze the data and dispense advice on how to improve your health and fitness. But that reliance on AI means you’ll need the right type of iPhone to enjoy all the benefits.

Also: Apple could build its AI health chatbot from this study – how to enroll

Here are five helpful new features built into the app, along with what you’ll need to access them.

First up, the app will offer suggestions based on data from different sources. For example, it might advise you to go for a walk at a nearby park if it detects that you’re not getting enough exercise. It may show you articles and videos about sleep if it finds that you’re not well-rested. It could also highlight possible conditions based on your lab and test results. You can easily view these recommendations from the Insights screen.

Also: Health is Tim Cook’s defining legacy – and your Apple Watch proves it

A new feature called Health Age compares your physical health to your actual age to show how you’re doing. The analysis draws on certain stats and lab data, such as your resting heart rate, sleep, heart rate variability (HRV), cholesterol, and A1C (average blood glucose levels), to deliver a health age, which may differ from your chronological age. The results can show you areas that may be of concern or that you need to focus on.

Also: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Finally, the health tracker I’ve been waiting for

Apple promises that the analysis is performed on your device without recording, storing, or sharing the video.

The new app will be able to correlate your test results with data collected by your iPhone and Apple Watch to give you a more comprehensive picture of your health. Plus, Apple and Quest Diagnostics have teamed up to offer people in the US an optional $119 bloodwork panel that covers more than 50 biomarkers to scan for different health and medical conditions.

Also: I tested the Apple Watch Series 12 heart-rate claims against my gold-standard Polar strap

Normally, you need an Apple Fitness+ subscription to fire up workout videos to help you exercise. But the new Health app will come with its own comprehensive set of training videos. Available from the Insights section, a series of strength exercise videos are designed to help you build your body strength. The videos cover all the key areas of your body to give you a full workout.

Some of the new features, such as the strength videos, will be available to all iPhone users. But the ones that rely on AI will run only on phones that support Apple Intelligence. That means you’ll need an iPhone 15 Pro or Pro Max, any iPhone 16 or 17, an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max, an iPhone Air, or an iPhone Duo.

#2984. Why TSMC Stock Soared Today

AI stocks jumped on news of Jensen Huang's return.

By Jeremy Bowman – Nov 23, 2026 at 4:00PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ›

Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation (TSM +14.09%) (TSMC) were soaring today, as it was one of the biggest winners on the news that Jensen Huang was returning as CEO of Nvidia.

TSMC is the world's biggest chip manufacturer and Nvidia's exclusive manufacturing partner. It also produces more than 90% of the world's most advanced chips.

Investors rushed back into AI stocks on the news, with TSMC up 14.5% and the Nasdaq Composite gaining 6.9%.

As the world's biggest chip manufacturer with a majority share of contract chips, TSMC is the linchpin of the semiconductor industry and is highly exposed to both the health of that industry and the success of AI more generally.

Nvidia is now its biggest customer, reportedly accounting for 19% of its revenue in 2025, so the success of Nvidia is also key for TSMC.

Jensen Huang has been the mastermind behind Nvidia's dominance of AI chips and the biggest champion of AI more broadly, and investors were fearful that the industry would lose much of its momentum and stability without him.

His return makes investors more confident in Nvidia's growth, which benefits TSMC, and reassures them about the broader strength of the AI sector.

At TSMC, 68% of its revenue now comes from high-performance computing, much of which is data center AI chips, so AI has become the biggest driver of its business.

Recently, reports emerged that Nvidia had asked TSMC to consider manufacturing 3D memory chips, which would be an entirely new business for TSMC, as it has historically only made logic components.

It's unclear whether anything will come of that proposal, but it shows the potential for growth in the Nvidia-TSMC relationship.

Demand for AI chips continues to outstrip supply, which is good news for TSMC. The stock still looks well-priced at a price-to-earnings ratio of 23.6.

The company says the electrified system is both more efficient and more powerful than the current nonhybrid versions. For buyers who want a more battery-focused experience, Genesis teased an upcoming 640-mile extended-range electric vehicle due to arrive in early 2027.

The hybridized versions of the brand’s most popular sedan and SUV arrive as American drivers show growing interest in energy-efficient cars, both battery electrics and hybrids, driven by high fuel costs and better understanding of the technologies. Hybrids, in particular, have attracted attention because they behave like traditional combustion cars: There’s no need to install home charging hardware or change familiar driving and refueling habits. Genesis says the system is 16% more powerful than the gasoline-only version, outputting 347 horsepower and 391 pound-feet of torque. Genesis hasn’t announced official fuel economy estimates, but says the G80 Hybrid is 30% more efficient than the standard model, while the GV80 Hybrid is 24% more efficient. Based on current EPA figures, my math puts them in the ballpark of 30 mpg and 27 mpg, respectively. Any improvement is good, but those aren’t exactly earth-shattering gains. We’ll have to wait for the official ratings to be sure.

Each hybrid can be toggled into a silent EV mode for short distances — good for gliding into a driveway, garage or parking deck without waking the neighbors. However, without a plug, all the energy in the battery ultimately comes from the gas tank.

A new Stay Mode lets owners run the climate control and infotainment without starting the engine for around 30 minutes. I like to think of it as the “moment of zen in the driveway before you have to go inside and face responsibility” mode, or maybe the “eating lunch in your car” mode. It’s similar to Toyota’s My Room Mode on its hybrids.

Aside from the powertrain, the G80 and GV80 Hybrids are largely identical to their combustion counterparts. Hybrid-specific touches include a three-dimensional G-Matrix grille inlay redesigned for these models, as well as new exterior colors.

Inside, a 27-inch OLED display combining the instrument cluster and navigation stretches halfway across the dashboard. Tech features include Digital Key 2 Premium, which lets owners use their phone instead of a key fob to unlock and start the car, and active road noise cancellation. Genesis’ driver-assistance suite is headlined by the Highway Drive Assist 2 steering assistance system and the Remote Smart Parking Assist 2, which enables automatic parking with the driver inside or just nearby the car.

Prices for the sedan and SUV haven’t been announced. Final specifications and EPA fuel economy figures are expected closer to the early 2027 launch window.

My cynical side says that these new models are just Genesis doing what Toyota has done since the RX 400h debuted in 2004. (To be fair, Genesis didn’t become an independent brand until 2015, so its rival has a bit of a head start.) In practical terms, the move brings Hyundai Motor Group’s luxury brand into parity with other group members and luxury car competitors that have rolled out updated hybrids over the last year, and meets customers’ increasing demand for more energy-efficient cars where they are.

In addition to its first hybrid sedan and SUV, Genesis executives announced that the brand will expand the availability of its wild-styled, high-performance GV60 Magma full-electric SUV to more states and markets to meet higher-than-expected demand.

At the debut event in LA, the brand also teased an upcoming extended-range EV — an EV with an onboard gasoline generator, essentially a very advanced plug-in hybrid — set to launch in early 2027. The EREV model is targeting over 640 miles before its “all-new high-performance battery” and gas tank both run dry, but Genesis didn’t give further details about the upcoming model.

Editor’s note: Antuan Goodwin’s travel costs were covered by Genesis. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Mobile OS > iOS

The new Google Wallet app brings Gemini agentic shopping to US-based iOS users - sorry, no tap-to-pay.

The Google Wallet app is available for iPhone users in the US for the first time. iOS users who download the new Google Wallet app can manage online payments for faster checkout at places that support Google Pay. However, Apple restricts Google’s ability to offer tap-to-pay service on the iOS app, so users won’t be able to use Google Wallet for contactless checkout on iPhone.

Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits

The new Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes. Google Wallet app users on iOS will also be able to view receipts and track orders pulled from Gmail in one app.

There used to be a Google Pay app for iOS, but it was discontinued in 2024. The old Google Pay app also didn’t support tap-to-pay on iPhone, but it offered limited functionality, including support for loyalty and gift cards, as well as purchase tracking.

The biggest difference between the old Google Pay app for iOS and the new Google Wallet is the AI component, which supports agentic shopping, likely as Google’s longer-term play.

One of Google’s goals for the Wallet app on iOS is to make it a central place to manage purchases made by its AI agents. The Agents section in Google Wallet for iPhone lets you manage and monitor purchases made through Gemini.

Agentic commerce is on the rise, as evidenced by the growing use of Meta’s Muse. Gemini can make purchases and payments through the Tasks feature, which lets you give Gemini permission to buy the items you want and set your maximum budget.

Also: Google Wallet just turned your Android phone into a digital house key

The Google Wallet app for iOS becomes the central hub for purchase management in agentic commerce through Gemini. In it, you can view active tasks to see which purchases Gemini is working on, as well as completed purchases and receipts.

Google has been working on two technologies to support its agentic commerce strategy: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2).

UCP is a technical language that enables AI agents to communicate with retailers and make purchases, while AP2 is the payment framework that establishes rules and authorization for agents to make payments.

Google Wallet serves as both the AI-powered wallet and the consumer-facing record of transactions made by Gemini.

Also: Google Wallet has a lot of new tricks – these 5 are my favorites

Along with Google, major retailers supported the development of UCP, including Shopify, Walmart, Target, and Etsy. When Google announced AP2, more than 60 organizations became involved, including PayPal, Salesforce, Mastercard, and American Express.

#2981. Andrew Garfield on Becoming Sam Altman in ‘Artificial’: ‘I’m Dying to Understand This Person’

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

At an SFFilm screening of the biopic, the actor tells CNET about the physical and mental process of trying to grasp the "central truths" about OpenAI's CEO.

It’s a tall order for an actor to embody any living person, but especially someone whom audiences may already have negative feelings about.

Rather than daunting, that challenge was “exciting” to actor Andrew Garfield, who plays OpenAI’s polarizing CEO Sam Altman in the film Artificial, slated for an initial Dec. 25 release. The biopic follows the rise of OpenAI, focusing on Altman’s relationships — particularly with his cofounder Ilya Sutskever (Yura Borisov) — as he relentlessly pursues success amid Silicon Valley’s artificial intelligence power struggle.

Garfield’s perspective on Altman morphed as he worked to better understand him, the actor told me ahead of an early screening hosted by SFFilm in the heart of the city where the story is set. His mission as an actor is to get to the “central truths” of who a person is, he said, “and try to merge my soul with theirs. And like all of us, Sam has so many facets.”

That includes physical traits. Garfield says he had to lose weight and change his gait and voice to try to match Altman’s. The semblance is striking. From his bouncy stride to his clipped, gravelly speech, Garfield effortlessly emulates the Altman we’ve seen in interviews and Congressional testimonies. It’s a remarkable transformation — down to the sly, coaxing glint in his eyes — showcasing the breadth of Garfield’s acting talent.

But it goes beyond physicality. Garfield had to dig deep internally to find elements “that felt like they were a match” with Altman, he said. The result is an astonishingly believable portrayal of a multidimensional figure, at once pensive and inscrutable.

“There is a responsibility,” Garfield told me. “I take it very, very seriously to play any character, but particularly someone who’s alive, someone who’s pretty much my age. But also, maybe the greater responsibility is making sure that we interrogate these human beings that are leading our world into the next chapter, it seems.”

“And it feels like our job as storytellers to reflect the times we’re in,” he added, “and no better way of doing that than by looking at the human beings — their personal relationships, their souls, all the diamond facets of their souls — and interrogate the people that have the power over our culture right now.”

Artificial explores OpenAI’s rise through a rather bleak lens, with questions of moral responsibility and safety looming over the protagonists as they navigate the company’s success. The film is laced with dark satire, which offers moments of levity amid otherwise weighty meditations on the technology’s long-term impact.

In one scene, when Sutskever is asked about the difference between AI and artificial general intelligence, which can theoretically match or even surpass human ability, he plainly responds, “It’s like how rocket ships are different from scooters.” He goes on to tell his cohorts that this is achievable “in your lifetime — well, maybe not yours or yours or yours,” as he points to the less youthful figures in the room. Moments like these elicited generous laughter from the audience.

Director Luca Guadagnino, known for deeply character-driven stories, such as Challengers and Call Me by Your Name, said he was following the news about Sam Altman’s temporary ousting from OpenAI in 2023 and was fascinated by the “Shakespearean feud” leading to that moment. Guadagnino applies his signature character-centric approach to OpenAI’s story, relying on slow, measured beats, piercing close-ups and suspenseful music to relay the stakes of each pivotal moment.

“It’s never about the object; it’s always about the people,” Guadagnino said during a panel discussion after the screening. “It’s not about AGI or AI. It’s about the conflict between worldview and way of being, embodied by people that clash or fight for the vision they have.”

He also said, “The point for me was more about trying to understand: How did the possibility of an incredible technology that can help all of us turn into the opportunity to get power in your hands and to become self-entitled?”

Garfield is no stranger to portraying prominent figures in the tech world, having played Eduardo Saverin, Facebook’s co-founder and former chief financial officer, in 2010’s The Social Network. On the surface, Artificial seems like a spiritual successor, recounting another defining moment in the tech industry. But the films differ in both tone and approach, with Artificial trading rapid-fire drama for a darker, more existential theme that occasionally ventures into more technical territory. What the films do share is a focus on bold, forceful personalities.

“From that experience, I suppose, I was very curious about what it takes to win in this particular late-stage capitalist world that we’re in with these emerging technologies,” Garfield said during the panel discussion. “What does it take to hold Sauron’s Ring of Power and not be completely burnt up by it? Is it possible to not completely lose yourself to that overwhelming, exponentially growing possibility and power?”

Comic relief also arrives in the form of Ike Barinholtz playing OpenAI cofounder and tech mogul Elon Musk. By portraying him as a brutish, aloof figure who saunters in and out of rooms on a whim, he effectively underscores the absurdity of perceived importance and status. Almost every on-screen moment generated a murmur of laughter in the audience.

“I think we’re all fascinated by these cultural, iconic figures who are leading us into this next stage of culture and society,” Garfield told the crowd. “They’re kind of kids. They’re kind of slightly stuck in an early developmental place, and that felt like a really important part of Luca’s telling of this story.”

In fact, he added, “[Guadagnino] would say to us, ‘This is a John Hughes movie. This is a high school, screwball comedy, just with slightly higher stakes — mixed in with a little bit of Invasion of the Body Snatchers.’ A very important part of this is that these are all kind of adolescent, high-school-minded people.”

Even the way Garfield portrays Altman flippantly perching on couches and sitting cross-legged on tabletops while donning sunglasses — including during serious conversations about the future of OpenAI — was deeply researched.

“We had amazing consultants and researchers that work with us that gave us lots of information that’s not quite in the public arena about our characters,” Garfield said. “And Sam is someone who apparently would always sit like he was crisscross applesauce at play school, nursery school [or] kindergarten.”

Ultimately, Artificial poses an open question about where society is headed and whether those at the helm are equipped to lead the charge. Amid weighty explorations of AI’s ramifications, the film paints a haunting, revelatory portrait of the cunning, mercurial figures making decisions that shape our world.

For Garfield, this presented an opportunity to dive deep into a figure like Altman, who, despite his prominence, remains largely elusive in the public eye.

“I just wanted to tell this story and actually uncover for myself, excavate for myself, who is this person?” Garfield told me. “I’m dying to understand this person, and I get to try to understand this person, maybe more than anyone else has ever really tried to. And it feels like a gift to me.”

#2979. 90% of employers reject resumes that look like AI – yet half use AI to interview

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

In today's job market, do applicants really have a choice of whether to comply with AI hiring tools?

Hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider. At the same time, they’re turning to AI to help screen more candidates — meaning those videos you’ve seen on the internet of people pranking AI interviewers aren’t going away anytime soon.

New data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.

Also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI? This dashboard tracks the cuts – and the cost

“The survey data is self-reported, so it reflects what employers believe has happened, not a measured outcome,” Greenhouse’s Head of Voice AI Ophir Samson told ZDNET via email.

Employers are also reacting to AI by adjusting their hiring processes: 86% of those surveyed reported changes to account for AI’s impact. 57% of them did so by adding another human interview.

“As jobseekers rely more on AI to polish and send out their job applications, employers are finding it harder to tell who’s actually right for the role,” the report stated, echoing an ongoing push-and-pull between applicants and hiring teams. AI resume screeners automatically toss a majority of applications they deem unfit, so applicants try not to get tossed by formatting their material for the screener, which then backfires anyway.

The report shows how a tough economy and an influx of AI hiring tools are colliding, arguably to benefit employers over applicants. Greenhouse noted that, ironically, AI tools are helping hiring managers while also making resumes untrustworthy, and applicants would rather be interviewed by AI than not at all.

Also: How to beat the AI algorithm and get the job of your dreams

“A growing number of employers are using AI not just to filter candidates out, but to have conversations with more candidates, earlier, through AI-powered voice technology,” Greenhouse said, adding that “half now use AI interviews to hear from more candidates, and 40% of those have found strong candidates they would have missed.”

Greenhouse itself offers a voice AI screening interview tool. Samson told ZDNET that an HR professional ran 200 candidates she’d rejected through Greenhouse’s tool, and it suggested 19.

“All five of the finalists came from that group, and she ultimately hired one from the group,” Samson said.

What we don’t, and maybe can’t, know is the inverse: whether AI screeners influence hiring managers to turn away candidates they actually should have considered. At least in Greenhouse’s case, Samson said Voice AI doesn’t make hiring decisions or “automatically advance, reject, or rank candidates.”

“Recruiters review every output, and one recruiter owns the outcome and can explain how they reached it,” he said.

Greenhouse’s report surveyed 1,347 hiring managers and recruiters across the US, UK, Germany, Australia, and Ireland from late September to mid-October, and found that half of employers using voice AI “say the early-stage candidate experience has improved.”

Also: ‘So perfect, they are literally identical’ – Your AI-polished resumes are recruiters’ new top stressor

It’s unclear what “improved” means there, though, and whether applicants themselves would agree with that. Still, when given the choice, only 7% of applicants in the US would turn down an AI interview, per an earlier Greenhouse report. Additionally, “70% of those who’ve had a live AI interview say it helped them show their skills,” that report said.

But how swayed is that by the state of the US job market? October’s job report was better than expected, but it’s still been a tough year overall for job-seekers. Greenhouse’s findings could be as much a reflection of how desperate applicants are as an endorsement of or comfort with AI screenings.

“The job market could be a factor. Our Future of Hiring Candidate Report shows 81% of job seekers were rejected from a job in the past year without speaking to anyone at the company, human or AI,” Samson said. “But I’d be careful about reading the data as desperation. Candidates are setting clear conditions: nearly half (49%) want to know if a human will review their responses and 40% want to know how they’ll be evaluated.”

Also: Why replacing staff with AI backfires – and 5 ways smart leaders generate real value instead

Samson said that a software engineer named Ryan Quinlan, who was hired at Blissway, initially thought “talking to an AI” sounded stranger, but that it ultimately “felt like a conversation” that let him mention skills he’d forgotten to include on his resume. Samson said that Ryan has been “a ‘maybe’ on paper,” but that the AI interview helped him get over the line to be considered.

“For most applicants, a human conversation was never on the table,” Samson said. “The real choice is a resume lost in a pile, or 15 minutes to tell their story.”

Greenhouse found that while employers are using AI to screen more candidates, most are maintaining human oversight over the most important decisions in the hiring process.

“Of all the tasks employers would hand to an AI agent, deciding which candidates to advance came last, at just 7%,” Greenhouse said.

A recent California law aims to protect employees from being fired by AI systems that make determinations about their performance without a human co-signing the assessment. As with many AI productivity tools in the workplace, proper adoption ideally equates to more time for human workers to handle more important tasks.

Also: 92% of HR say staff can train for AI jobs – but half of companies still hire outside

“Of employers who’ve saved time with AI, 85% put it back into candidates, most often by spending more time with shortlisted candidates (45%) and interviewing more candidates earlier (40%),” Greenhouse said.

The main question around AI interviewers remains whether they’re correctly capturing your interview the way you’d hope a human interviewer would (though that’s still deeply subjective and out of applicants’ control anyway).

“When AI interviews are implemented thoughtfully and transparently, they pay off for both candidates and recruiters,” Samson said. “Every candidate who uses our Voice AI can opt out, and about 90% rate the experience as excellent.”

The recently renovated Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort offers great views, a well-equipped fitness center and delicious food.

Hilton is making a big play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort. The massive 1,000-room property — which underwent an $80 million renovation before opening under the Signia Hilton brand in May 2026 — sits on the beach in Hollywood, Florida, just outside of Fort Lauderdale.

The resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R. The main downside: The location isn’t great if your trip primarily revolves around off-property excursions, dining and nightlife.

Room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable. There’s also a resort fee of $59 per night — but Hilton waives that when you book using Hilton points.

Hilton covered the cost of my stay for two nights, but the opinions in this review are my own. Here’s what guests can expect at this oceanfront resort.

Since the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort is part of Hilton Honors, there are several ways to book a stay there.

If you’re using Hilton points, expect to pay 70,000 to 80,000 points a night when standard rooms are available. Hilton elite status — a benefit you can earn by holding any Hilton Honors credit card — gets you the fifth-night-free perk, where you stay for at least five nights but pay for four when booking with points.

For example, if you were to stay five nights at 80,000 points a night, you’d pay 320,000 points total, bringing down your average nightly rate to 64,000 points.

You can also book using Hilton’s generous free night certificates, which can be used at almost any property in the portfolio. If you hold the Hilton Honors American Express Aspire Card, you automatically get a certificate each year. It’s also possible to earn certificates through reaching spending thresholds on the card and on the Hilton Honors American Express Surpass® Card. Terms apply.

Make sure to check the cash rate against the points rate to make sure you’re getting good value from your redemption. NerdWallet values Hilton points at 0.4 cent apiece.

For cash bookings of two nights or more, you might consider using The Hotel Collection via American Express’ travel portal for eligible cardholders. Eligible bookings come with benefits like a $100 property credit and other amenities subject to availability, including a room upgrade, early check-in and late checkout.

Keep in mind that third-party bookings typically don’t earn Hilton points or count toward elite status qualification.

It’s hard to miss the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort, with its signature H-shaped facade and sleek white-and-glass exterior.

Stepping into the hotel, I was immediately struck by the lush greenery filling the entrance and indoor courtyard. The grand lobby has soaring glass ceilings, giving the space a greenhouse feel, although the strong air conditioning keeps you cool.

Despite its massive size, it doesn’t have a sprawling layout, which I appreciated. Everything is close together, and you can walk from the check-in counter to any of the indoor restaurants in under a minute.

I stayed in an oceanfront suite with a balcony, which was spacious and had a fun beachy vibe. To get to the rooms, you’ll need to use either the north or south tower elevator banks.

In the living room, there was a large sitting area featuring a TV, a couch, an accent chair and a four-person high-top table.

Although I didn’t spend too much time on the balcony — the October balminess was a bit too much for me — I enjoyed stepping out each morning to admire the view.

The bedroom had a king bed with extremely comfortable bedding and an oversized chair that was a great spot to relax and read a book by the window.

The bathroom was spacious, featuring a shower and a separate tub (something every room has).

Even the standard room I toured felt roomy. I liked that it shared similar elements with the suite, including the oversized lounge chair.

This is what you’d normally get when booking a room at the cheapest points price.

There are several dining venues on the property, ranging from a grab-and-go cafe to a high-end steakhouse. It is a luxury resort, so expect the prices to reflect that.

For breakfast, you can head to Palmea Kitchen, which is also open for lunch. I had the breakfast buffet, which offered a nice spread of classics, from hot food items and pastries to cold cuts and smoked salmon.

If you don’t have time for a sit-down breakfast, you can head next door to The Press, which offers made-to-order and grab-and-go food options throughout the day. You can also get smoothies, juices, snacks, pastries and other sweet treats.

The Canteen is another grab-and-go option that also sells snacks, drinks, souvenirs and sundries, similar to a convenience store.

For lunch and dinner, try Solara. It doesn’t have a traditional restaurant feel, as it’s mostly an indoor-outdoor bar space. One side connects to the lobby, while the other side faces the Solara adults-only pool.

It serves a lunch menu, as well as a substantial bar food menu that’s available late into the night.

You can also eat at Playa Beach Bar & Grill, a beachside restaurant serving Latin-inspired cuisine. I enjoyed spending a lazy lunch there and watching the waves crash onto the shore.

For a fancy sit-down dinner, go to Diplomat Prime, the property’s steakhouse. We had a group dinner at the restaurant, and the meats were, of course, the highlight. But don’t sleep on the seafood, which was also delicious.

One of the best parts of the Dip, as it’s affectionately known, is its location right on the beach. Guests can access the stretch of beach directly adjacent to the property. But it’s not a private beach, so you might encounter crowds.

I didn’t spend any time on the beach itself — it was extremely windy while I was there — but the hotel’s resort fee includes amenities like a beach lounge (umbrella not included), a daily one-hour kayak or paddleboard rental, and beachfront yoga classes.

If you don’t want to get sand everywhere, you can head to one of the three pool options: the adults-only Solara pool, the family-friendly lagoon pool and the Verandah Social Club for those 21 and older (requires paid access).

The family-friendly lagoon spans the length of the property and runs beneath the Solara pool. It also has its own hot tub.

I spent an afternoon in a cabana at the Verandah Social Club, which has some smaller plunge pools and a hot tub.

I appreciated the attentive service from the staff there, who constantly checked on whether guests needed anything.

If you’re looking for other ways to stay active, head to the two-story fitness center, featuring a variety of equipment like free weights, exercise bikes, a rowing machine and treadmills.

Next door, you’ll find the spa and wellness center. I had a relaxing massage that incorporated hot stones and aromatherapy.

The locker rooms come with a sauna and steam room, although I wished there were more amenities like a hot tub and cold plunge.

One of the resort fee inclusions is complimentary high-intensity interval training workout classes at the gym across the street. I signed up for an early morning class. The instructor was friendly, and it was a great way to start my day.

Other amenities include a complimentary one-hour e-bike rental each day, as well as a kids’ club with various activities (but drop-off fees apply).

I had a fantastic stay at this resort, but I’d recommend it for a specific traveler.

If you’re planning to stay on-property your entire trip, it’s a great option. That’s probably why it’s such a popular convention hotel, since everything you need is easily accessible.

I loved the hotel’s design, including the jungle-like atmosphere in the lobby, and I found the dining options to be tasty, albeit pricey.

But if your trip revolves around visiting Miami attractions, you’ll likely want to stay closer to the action.
